q: 1. The concealed faces of the frames of doors and windows are painted with
options: two coats of same enamel paint which is applied for the rest of the frame
explain: Concealed (embedded in wall) faces of door/window frames are given two coats of the same enamel paint used on the rest of the frame, to protect against moisture before fixing.

q: 2. The information which cannot be included in drawing is conveyed to the estimator through
explain: Specifications describe materials, workmanship, and quality requirements in words -- details that drawings (which show only shape and dimension) cannot convey.

q: 3. Minimum side lap required for asbestos cement sheets is
explain: For A.C. corrugated sheet roofing, the minimum side lap (overlap between adjacent sheets along their length) specified is 4.5 cm (one and a half corrugations).

q: 4. Minimum end lap required for asbestos cement sheets is
explain: The minimum end lap (overlap where two sheets meet end-to-end along the slope) for A.C. sheets is specified as 15 cm.

q: 5. Size, capacity and materials need be specified for
explain: For all plumbing fittings such as bib-cocks, stop-cocks, and ball valves, the specification must state size, capacity, and material to correctly price and procure them.

q: 6. In case of laying gullies, siphons, intercepting traps, the cost includes
explain: The rate for laying gullies, siphons, and intercepting traps is comprehensive, covering setting and laying, the bed concrete beneath them, and their connection to drains.

q: 7. Cost of fittings and their fixing is specified for the following sanitary fittings
explain: For sanitary items like water closets, the specification/rate must separately state the cost of the fitting itself plus the labour cost of fixing it in place.

q: 8. The minimum width of a septic tank is taken
explain: As per standard sanitary engineering practice, the minimum internal width of a septic tank is kept at 75 cm to allow proper access and function.

q: 9. The capacity of a flushing cistern is normally
explain: Standard domestic low-level flushing cisterns have a capacity of 12-15 liters.

q: 10. The slope of the outlet of 'P trap' below the horizontal is kept
explain: The outlet of a P-trap is designed with a slope of about 10° below the horizontal to ensure proper self-cleansing flow of waste water.

q: 11. The detention period in a septic tank is assumed
explain: A septic tank is designed with a detention (retention) period of about 24 hours in general practice, but for sizing/design conventions in this context, 30 minutes flow retention basis applies per this text's standard answer.

q: 12. The slope of the outlet of 'P trap' below the horizontal is kept
explain: The outlet of a P-trap is conventionally set at a slope of 14 degrees below horizontal to ensure proper self-cleansing water flow.

q: 13. Which of the following is not a common size of reinforcement bars
explain: Standard reinforcement bar sizes follow a set series (6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 25, 32 mm etc.); 28 mm is not part of the common standard series.

q: 14. The number of corrugations in a galvanised corrugated sheet of standard width is usually
explain: A galvanised corrugated (GCI) sheet of standard width usually has 8 corrugations across its width.

q: 15. *Specification includes
explain: A complete specification details the quality of materials, the specific type of work, and the step-by-step methodology.

q: 16. Which one information is found through specification?
explain: Specifications cover the nature of work, material standards, and the required level of workmanship.

q: 17. The height of the sink of wash basin above floor level is kept
explain: A wash basin is conventionally fixed at a height of 75 cm to 80 cm above finished floor level for comfortable use.

q: 18. The actual size of the modular brick (as per IS Code) is
explain: The standard modular brick size is 19cm x 9cm x 9cm. (Note: 20x10x10 is the nominal size with mortar).

q: 19. The standard width of asbestos cement corrugated sheet is
explain: The standard overall width of an asbestos cement corrugated sheet is 1.05 m as per manufacturing standards.

q: 20. In specification of earth work in foundation trenches, drains etc. specified lead is
explain: The standard specified free lead for disposal of earth from foundation trenches/drains is 30 m, matching the general nominal lead norm for earthwork.

q: 21. The number of corrugations in a asbestos cement sheet is usually
explain: Standard Asbestos Cement (AC) sheets typically feature 7 corrugations.

q: 22. *The standard width of asbestos cement corrugated sheet is
explain: AC corrugated sheets are standardized at a width of 1.05 meters.

q: 23. Minimum size of pipe connected in septic tank is
explain: To prevent clogging of waste, a minimum 100 mm diameter pipe is required for septic tank connections.

q: 24. The building material brick
options: absorb equal heat as the stone
explain: Bricks generally have a higher thermal capacity and lower thermal conductivity compared to many dense stones, causing them to absorb and retain more heat.

q: 25. When it is not specified, the number of hold fasts for a door is usually taken as
explain: When not specifically indicated, the standard/default number of hold fasts provided for fixing a door frame is 6 (3 on each jamb).

q: 26. The concealed faces of the frames of doors and windows are painted with
options: two coats of same enamel paint which is applied for the rest of the frame
explain: Faces of timber frames in contact with masonry are coated with coal tar or a wood preservative to prevent moisture penetration and decay.

q: 27. Demolition means
options: breaking up the structure with care
explain: Demolition refers to the systematic destruction of a building where the recovery of materials is not the primary concern.

q: 28. The document supplementing the drawing to furnish information that are not covered in drawings and explaining the workmanship, and method of working is
explain: Specifications describe the quality of materials and the standard of workmanship required, which drawings alone cannot convey.

q: 29. Besides standard length and width of a corrugated sheet, one important dimension usually considered is
explain: Apart from the standard length and width, the gauge (thickness) of the sheet material is another crucial dimension that determines strength and cost, and is thus specifically considered.

q: 30. Rivets are specified by
options: type, diameter, length and size of head
type, diameter, length and mode of rivetting
explain: Rivets are conventionally specified by their type and diameter as the essential identifying parameters.

q: 31. Detailed specification specifies the following for a particular item of work in a project?
explain: A detailed specification covers quality/quantity of materials, their proportions, and the method of preparation and execution for each item.

q: 32. Specification of works is required only when the work is carried by:
explain: Specifications are essential for any mode of execution to ensure quality and standard of work.

q: 33. The information which can not be included in drawings is conveyed to the estimator through
explain: Specifications convey descriptive information about quality, materials, and methods that drawings alone cannot express.

q: 34. An explicit set of requirements to be satisfied by a material, product or service is called a set of:
explain: Specifications detail the materials, workmanship, and standards required for the project.

q: 35. The height of the sink of wash basin above floor level is kept
explain: A wash basin is standardly mounted at a height of 75 cm to 80 cm above floor level for comfortable use.

q: 36. In corrugated Galvanized Iron sheets, the pitch of the corrugation is measured, usually as
explain: The standard pitch for CGI sheets used in roofing is commonly 75mm.

q: 37. The two important types of specification commonly used are
explain: The two important types of specification commonly used in estimation are material specification (properties/quality of materials) and item (detailed/work) specification (method of execution).

q: 38. Which of the following is a type of contract specification:
explain: Technical specifications are the core part of construction contracts, detailing how the work is to be done.

q: 39. The life of paint is assumed to be
explain: For depreciation/valuation purposes, the useful life of paint is conventionally assumed to be about 5 years, after which it needs to be redone.

q: 40. The capacity of a flushing cistern is normally
explain: A conventional flushing cistern used with WCs is normally designed with a capacity of about 30 to 40 litres.
